name: Syria
summary: Became independent from France in 1946; ruled by the Assad family from 1970; a civil war began in 2011 and Assad fell in December 2024.

knownFor.label: Damascus
knownFor.note: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

terrain.value: Fertile plains, high mountains, plateaus and deserts; the Euphrates crosses the east.

climate.value: Humid Mediterranean on the coast, semi-arid steppe inland and arid desert in the east.

resources.value: Petroleum, natural gas, phosphate rock and arable land.

disasters.value: A record drought helped cause a severe hunger crisis in 2025.

urbanisation.value: Damascus (the capital and largest city) and Aleppo, among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

disease.value: The civil war severely damaged the health care system.

migration.value: The civil war from 2011 caused a refugee crisis, with over 5 million refugees and millions more displaced inside Syria.

economicBase.value: Mainly farming before the civil war began in 2011; also oil.

tradeRoutes.value: Old caravan routes; port of Latakia.

wealth.value: Much poorer since the war: GDP shrank by 84% (2010–23) and over 90% of people live in poverty.

moneyAndTax.value: The Syrian pound, which lost 80% of its value during the war.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: Governed by a transitional government since March 2025, after the fall of the Assad regime (December 2024).

keyRulers.value: Shukri al-Quwatli. Hafez al-Assad. Bashar al-Assad.

succession.value: Many coups (1949–71), then rule by the Assad family until 2024.

institutions.value: The Ba’ath Party ran a one-party state from 1963 until the fall of Assad in 2024.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Army; many armed groups during the war.

territoryChange.value: The western two-thirds of the Golan Heights have been occupied by Israel since 1967.

alliancesRivals.value: Iran and Russia backed the Assad government in the civil war.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Ten public universities, led by Damascus University and the University of Aleppo.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Four international airports: Damascus, Aleppo, Latakia and Qamishli.

religion.value: About 74% Sunni Muslim, 10% Alawite and 10% Christian, with Shia and other minorities.

languageWriting.value: Arabic is official; most Kurds speak Kurmanji Kurdish.

artsArchitecture.value: Umayyad Mosque; old cities of Aleppo and Damascus.

socialStructure.value: Levantine Arabs are the largest group; Kurds are the second largest.

dailyLife.value: Dishes such as kibbeh, hummus, tabbouleh and shawarma.

colonisation.value: Ottoman rule from 1516; a French Mandate from 1920 until French troops left in 1946.

riseSignals.value: Independence: legally in 1945, with French troops leaving in April 1946.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
